title: Weak equivalences of Kan complexes give coherent-nerve equivalence edges
statement: Use Kan complexes, weak homotopy equivalences and equivalence edges of [def-cbc-enhanced-diagrams-cones], and let $\mathcal S_{\mathcal W}=N_{\mathrm{hc}}(\mathbf{Kan}_{\mathcal W})$ be the subset-poset coherent nerve defined in [def-coef-infinity-category-of-spaces]. Let $A,B$ be $\mathcal W$-small Kan complexes and let $f:A\to B$ be a simplicial map inducing a bijection on path components and isomorphisms on every based homotopy group after geometric realization. Regard $f$ as the edge from $A$ to $B$ in $\mathcal S_{\mathcal W}$ specified by its vertex in $\operatorname{Fun}(A,B)$. Then there exist a simplicial map $g:B\to A$ and two $2$-simplices of $\mathcal S_{\mathcal W}$ with vertex triples $(A,B,A)$ and $(B,A,B)$ and boundary arrows respectively $(f,g,1_A)$ and $(g,f,1_B)$. In particular this actual edge $f$ is an equivalence edge in the coherent-nerve convention. Empty and disconnected Kan complexes are allowed. The same edge and witnesses remain valid after inclusion in any containing value universe.

source.place: Agent extraction of the inverse-triangle construction in returned step 5 of lem-coef-infinity-pointwise-yoneda-evaluation; Kerodon Example 4.6.7.7 (06QR) for coherent-nerve mapping spaces and Subsection 4.6.8 (01PF) for composition and inverse triangles. The explicit subset-chain triangle argument is preserved in the delivery report. Kerodon identifiers, not Stacks tags; no Stacks theorem states this assertion.

proof.text: Apply [lem-cbc-kan-whitehead-inverse] to $f:A\to B$. Its hypotheses are precisely the two Kan conditions and the stated component and based homotopy-group conditions on the realization. It supplies a simplicial map $g:B\to A$ and simplicial homotopies $H:A\times\Delta^1\to A$ from $gf$ to $1_A$ and $J:B\times\Delta^1\to B$ from $fg$ to $1_B$. These are edges of the internal functor simplicial sets by their definition in [def-cbc-enhanced-diagrams-cones]. The cited inverse theorem explicitly permits empty and disconnected Kan complexes.

source.place: Proposition 3.1.7.13 (00UB), converse for Kan complexes; Corollary 3.6.4.3 (03X7) for the realization convention

proof.text: Apply [lem-coef-kan-coherent-nerve-inverse-equivalence] to the $\mathcal W$-small Kan complexes $A,B$, the maps $f$ and $g$ of step 1, and the simplicial homotopies $H$ between $gf$ and $1_A$ and $J$ between $fg$ and $1_B$; that statement allows either orientation of the homotopies, so $H$ and $J$ as given (from the composite to the identity) qualify, and it imposes no nonemptiness or connectedness hypothesis. It gives $2$-simplices $\sigma,\tau$ of $\mathcal S_{\mathcal W}$ with $\sigma|_{\Delta^{\{0,1\}}}=f$, $\sigma|_{\Delta^{\{1,2\}}}=g$, $\sigma|_{\Delta^{\{0,2\}}}=1_A$ and $\tau|_{\Delta^{\{0,1\}}}=g$, $\tau|_{\Delta^{\{1,2\}}}=f$, $\tau|_{\Delta^{\{0,2\}}}=1_B$; their vertex triples are $(A,B,A)$ and $(B,A,B)$. The edge $f$ there is the edge of $\mathcal S_{\mathcal W}$ given by the vertex $f$ of $\operatorname{Fun}(A,B)$, as in the statement, so this actual edge is an equivalence edge in the inverse-triangle sense of [def-cbc-enhanced-diagrams-cones].

source.place: Proposition 2.4.6.10 (00M5) with Remark 2.4.6.4 (00M0), as recorded in lem-coef-kan-coherent-nerve-inverse-equivalence (project inclusion-poset orientation)

proof.text: Let $\mathcal W\subseteq\mathcal W'$ be a containing value universe. The inclusion $\mathbf{Kan}_{\mathcal W}\to\mathbf{Kan}_{\mathcal W'}$ of [def-coef-infinity-category-of-spaces] is the identity on objects and on morphism simplicial sets $\operatorname{Fun}(S,T)$, hence an enriched functor. By [def-coef-coherent-nerve-infrastructure] the coherent nerve acts on enriched functors by postcomposition in every degree, and simplicial operators of the coherent nerve are restrictions along the enriched functors $\mathfrak C[\Delta^m]\to\mathfrak C[\Delta^n]$. Postcomposition commutes with these restrictions, so the images of $\sigma$ and $\tau$ in $\mathcal S_{\mathcal W'}$ have the same faces $f,g,1_A$ and $g,f,1_B$, and the image of the edge $f$ is the same vertex $f$ of $\operatorname{Fun}(A,B)$. Thus the same edge and witnesses remain valid after the inclusion.
